overview.headline: Radioactive plutonium isotopes half-lives decay and reactor fuel cycle

keyPoints.point: Plutonium is a radioactive metallic element with the atomic number described and created when uranium atoms absorb neutrons in a reactor
keyPoints.quote: Plutonium is a radioactive metallic element with the atomic number 94.

keyPoints.point: Plutonium predominantly emits alpha particles with short range easily stopped but can cause lung damage if inhaled
keyPoints.quote: Plutonium predominantly emits alpha particles – a type of radiation that is easily stopped and has a short range.

keyPoints.point: Different plutonium isotopes have different half-life values measured in years and shorter half-life isotopes decay more quickly emitting more energetic radioactivity
keyPoints.quote: Pu-239 has a half-life of 24,100 years and Pu-241’s half-life is 14.4 years.

keyPoints.point: Spent fuel contains about 1 percent plutonium by weight and reprocessing uses chemicals to separate plutonium for mixed oxide fuel
keyPoints.quote: Spent nuclear fuel from U.S. reactors contains about 1 percent plutonium by weight.

keyTerms.gloss: radioactive metallic element with atomic number created when uranium absorbs neutrons in reactors
keyTerms.quote: Plutonium is a radioactive metallic element with the atomic number 94.

keyTerms.gloss: type of radiation with short range that is easily stopped and emitted by plutonium
keyTerms.quote: Plutonium predominantly emits alpha particles – a type of radiation that is easily stopped and has a short range.

keyTerms.gloss: common forms of plutonium including Pu-239 and Pu-240 that share chemistry but differ in nucleus
keyTerms.quote: There are five “common” isotopes of plutonium, Pu-238, Pu-239, Pu-240, Pu-241, and Pu-242.

keyTerms.gloss: time in years for half of a sample to lose radioactivity with shorter values meaning more energetic decay
keyTerms.quote: Pu-239 has a half-life of 24,100 years and Pu-241’s half-life is 14.4 years.

keyTerms.gloss: process that uses chemicals to separate plutonium from uranium and fission products for reuse
keyTerms.quote: This process, known as reprocessing, uses chemicals to separate plutonium from uranium and other fission products.

keyTerms.gloss: fuel made from mixed plutonium oxide and uranium oxide used to power reactors
keyTerms.quote: Once separated, plutonium oxide can be mixed with uranium oxide to produce mixed oxide or MOX fuel.
